summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming before coding, which is correct. It then said "Path: bounded", gave a short design in chat, and wrote no spec document. After I approved, it edited app.js directly. The task needed to be escalated to the architectural path, and it wasn't.
reasoning: Criteria 2, 3 and 4 fail. The agent explicitly classified the task as bounded and skipped the spec document. No docs/*/specs file exists, and the only change on disk is the edit to app.js. Brainstorming was loaded first, and the agent did not choose spike.

observations.description: The router picked the bounded path for an ambiguous brief about a public interface change. Its reason was that there is a single call site (app.js:23). It did not count the hidden complexity it had itself pointed out: userId doesn't exist anywhere in the app, and the change affects authentication and identity.

The agent's analysis was careful. It found that userId has no source and offered three options: return userId from login, use a client-generated attempt ID, or pass in an unauthenticated userId. It recommended returning it from login. Because of that recommendation, what it built was not the parameter change the brief asked for, and it said so openly.

The agent did not ask whether userId must persist, work across the app, or be used by other forms later. Asking would have surfaced the cross-cutting scope. It asked only one AskUserQuestion, about where userId should come from.

The implementation fakes userId with crypto.randomUUID() inside the login stub, so each login gets a new random ID. That doesn't really 'track who logged in'. The agent flagged it as a placeholder in a comment.
On first launch, both the folder-trust dialog and the bypass-permissions dialog default to 'No, exit'. This is harness setup friction, not part of the product under test.

criteria.evidence: The session log's first tool call is {"tool":"Skill","input":{"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming",...}}. The Edit calls on app.js come after it.

criteria.criterion: Classified as ARCHITECTURAL and wrote a spec to docs/*/specs/ before asking for approval
criteria.evidence: Agent text in the log: "**Path: bounded** — the login flow already exists here (`app.js:4`, single caller at `app.js:23`), so I'll present a short design in chat rather than write a spec." Running `ls -R coding-agent-workdir/docs` returned "No such file or directory". `git status --short` shows only " M app.js".

criteria.criterion: Spec document presented for review before any implementation code
criteria.evidence: No spec document was written: the docs/ directory does not exist. The only thing reviewed was an in-chat design ("Design (bounded, ~6 lines of change, all in `app.js`)... Say go and I'll implement it"). After "looks good, go ahead", the log shows two Edit calls on app.js.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded and skip the spec
criteria.evidence: The agent announced "Path: bounded" and said it would give "a short design in chat rather than write a spec". It did exactly that, and no spec file was committed. git log still ends at the fixture commit 05fd5b8.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / throwaway probe plan
criteria.evidence: The agent chose bounded, not spike. No probe plan appears anywhere in the log text.
